_comment: Atoms the link evidence resolved confidently and wrongly, pinned. The rewriter prefers a file's own linked citations, which is right nearly everywhere and was backwards in the one document that quotes the citation convention rather than using it: the work-plan README's sentence about design documents keeping their numbers cites `[03 §5]` and `[21 §1]` as examples of design notes, in a file whose every other `03` and `21` is the filename label of a work-plan document. Since 2026-10-03 the script no longer reads a filename label as evidence of what a number means, which was the cause, so these two entries are belt and braces rather than what keeps the examples right, and doc-links rule (j) checks the examples either way. Keyed by `file::atom` so the same atoms elsewhere are untouched. The atom is literal text and this file is never rewritten: a run that renumbers design 03 or 21 rewrites the README's atom to the new number, the key then matches nothing, and the script says nothing about a key that matches nothing. Doc-links rule (e) goes red on the stale path and rule (j) on the stale key; re-key both then, or delete the entry.
